title: Octopus: 3 Dil, 9 Dimaag, Neela Khoon!
idea: An octopus has three hearts and copper-based blue blood, one heart pauses briefly when it swims, and about two-thirds of its 500 million neurons are in its arms.

lines.text: Is jaanwar ke teen dil hain, nau dimaag, aur khoon neela!
Do dil sirf gills ko khoon bhejte hain, teesra poori body ko.
Tairte waqt teesra dil pal bhar ruk jaata hai, shayad isliye kam tairta!

scene.small: Tairte waqt kuch pal ke liye

lines.text: Khoon mein iron nahi, copper wala hemocyanin hai, isliye rang neela!
Iske 50 crore neurons mein se do-tihai dimaag nahi, haathon mein hain!
Matlab har haath kaafi had tak khud sochta hai! Sabse ajeeb kya laga?

facts.claim: An octopus has three hearts: two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills, and one systemic heart pumps it to the rest of the body.
Octopus hearts stop for a few moments when it swims; one researcher thinks this may be why octopuses don't swim much.
Octopus blood is blue because it uses copper-based hemocyanin instead of iron-based hemoglobin.
Octopuses are often described as having nine brains: one central brain plus a cluster of nerve cells in each of the eight arms that helps control movement.
The common octopus has about 500 million neurons, and about two-thirds are in its arms (about 180 million in the central brain, more than 40 million in each arm).
